text: Business email compromise cost victims more than three billion dollars in 2025, according to the FBI. A vendor emails new bank details. Probity checks the request before the money moves, and every fact behind its decision is a query running in Zetaris.

note: The semantic layer: three sources, one USL
text: Our vendor master lives in Postgres. USAspending and the SEC's EDGAR are live public APIs. Zetaris registers all three as tables, and one compile turns them into a single semantic layer, vendor 360: twelve tables, three sources, one place to ask.

note: Live run: session table mid-check, re-run in Zetaris, lineage
text: This is a real run, not a replay. The agents read the letter, and the Registry Scout asks Zetaris for the vendor's corporate family. The letter's address belongs to a different Booz Allen entity, so the Registrar adds that entity to Zetaris as a session table, in the middle of the check. The Examiner will not accept the new link until it has re-run the query in Zetaris and the row hash matches. In the evidence drawer, every fact shows its lineage: source system, Zetaris table, query id, SQL hash and row hash.

note: Console: LIST DQ / RUN DQ, the sweep, one query across three systems
text: After the decision, a sweep of data-quality rules runs over the payment ledger. In the Zetaris console, LIST DQ shows the rules registered on the semantic layer, and RUN DQ flags payments whose bank account already belongs to another vendor. The newest rules found two vendors sharing one account. And one query across the ledger, USAspending and EDGAR returns the vendor's profile and its payment exposure in a single row.

Grok built this layer. It worked under a written contract, in slices, each logged with a UTC time. It read Zetaris's own agent rules, registered the sources, compiled the semantic layer and wrote the data-quality rules, checking each step against the live API. A later Grok pass added the three newest rules and the one-query profile, and another wrote the independent end-to-end tests. Where it could not verify something, the verdict file says so: seventeen of nineteen checks passed, two were left as not run. Claude Code built the agents and the interface.

note: Why it was amazing (the 40-60 s segment)
text: I needed the SEC's company filings inside a query. I wrote one statement, a REST table with the SEC's required header, and a real filing came back as a row in about five seconds. The second read took under two. I had written no connector. We estimate that saved an hour or more. Not everything was that easy. USAspending's API returned valid JSON, and Zetaris read it as one corrupt record, because the server sends a browser page unless you ask for application JSON. One header fixed it, but we lost time there. Then the moment it clicked. Grok wrote a test bank change into our live payment database, and I re-ran one data-quality rule. The invalid rows went from three to four, and it named the new payment item. No re-registration, no refresh, no pipeline. When the row was deleted, the count went back to three. Zetaris was reading Postgres in place. That rule is now the sweep Probity runs on every check.
Probity, from team Zen. Real runs, real Zetaris queries, and a row hash you can check yourself.
